lesson.text: Quick memory: who do you ask before you stroke a dog? (Its owner.) Today: saying hello to a dog, being a tree, bees and the farm.
Animals have feelings. Ask the owner first, then let the dog sniff the back of your hand, held low and still. Then stroke its side gently.
Leave dogs alone when they are eating or sleeping.
If a dog runs at you: be a tree. Stand still, fold your arms in, and look at your feet. Never run: running makes a dog chase.
A bee or a wasp buzzing near you? Walk away slowly, no swatting. A sting: tell a grown-up. On a farm, never walk behind a horse.
Try it in the world: open the practice park and the farm. Next: how a dog says 'leave me alone', on the Middle track.

choices: on the side or the back

exercises.prompt: Swatting a bee can make it sting.
Saying hello to a dog: put it in order.
items: let it sniff the back of your hand

exercises.prompt: A bee stung your friend. You...
You should walk behind a horse so it can't see you.
exercises.explain: False: walk at its side, where it can see you.

items: hugging a dog you don't know
exercises.explain: Asking and walking away are safe.

choices: still, arms folded in, looking at your feet
exercises.hint: Like a tree in the park.
